content.text: The text surveys Civil War campaigns from Shiloh through Chattanooga. Confederate forces initially drove Union troops at Shiloh, but gunboats and reinforcements crossing the Tennessee River secured a Union victory. It then recounts the fall of Memphis, Farragut’s capture of New Orleans, McClellan’s advance up the Peninsula, and battles at Fair Oaks and during the Seven Days’ retreat to Harrison’s Landing. Jackson’s movements through the Shenandoah Valley diverted Union forces, while Lee defeated Pope at Second Bull Run. Lee’s invasion of Maryland ended at Antietam, after which Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation. Grant captured Vicksburg and Port Hudson, severing the Confederacy. Gettysburg halted Lee’s invasion, while Chickamauga forced Rosecrans into Chattanooga, where Grant later relieved the siege.
